findings.issue_text: In scheduleEmailReminders.ts:48-77, if client.request throws for any single reminder, the catch swallows the error and Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete) is never reached, so all DB deletions for that run are skipped — cancelled rows are re-processed every run and reminders whose send time arrives before a successful run will still be sent

In scheduleEmailReminders.ts:43, the cancellation window is scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour but this endpoint is the only thing that actually cancels 'cancelled' email reminders at SendGrid; if the cron/endpoint doesn't run or runs late, a reminder marked cancelled: true will still be sent when its send time arrives — the cancel is only advisory until the batch job executes

In emailReminderManager.ts:210-222, the immediateDelete path (used by workflow deletion and step deletion) cancels the reminder at SendGrid but never deletes the DB record due to an early return, leaving orphaned WorkflowReminder rows that accumulate forever

On reschedule, email reminders are cancelled with immediateDelete: true (SendGrid cancel, no DB delete) while SMS reminders go through deleteScheduledSMSReminder which cancels Twilio and deletes the DB row — asymmetric handling leaves the old booking's email reminder rows in the DB pointing at a booking that no longer exists

The refactor removed await Promise.all(remindersToDelete); all deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder calls are fire-and-forget inside forEach. In the reschedule flow new reminders can be scheduled before old ones are deleted with no ordering guarantee, and failures are silently dropped since the functions swallow errors via console.log

In handleNewBooking.ts:963-971, the try/catch around the forEach is ineffective because the reminder-deletion functions are async — rejections become unhandled promise rejections, not caught exceptions, so the log.error('Error while canceling scheduled workflow reminders') path never fires for actual failures

In workflows.tsx (eventType disable path ~line 372-380), the refactor removed the ownership filter from reminder deletion; previously deleteMany filtered by booking.userId = ctx.user.id, but now deletion happens inside the reminder managers with no user check, relying solely on the upstream query for user ownership

In schema.prisma:644, the cancelled Boolean? column is nullable with no default; new reminders are created without setting cancelled so rows are NULL rather than false, and queries must remember to use cancelled: true vs undefined — a non-null default (false) would be safer and match the existing scheduled/scheduledDate columns

In scheduleEmailReminders.ts:53, cancellations are executed with sequential awaits inside a for loop rather than in parallel, slowing the endpoint when many reminders are pending and widening the race window with send times

No tests were added or updated for the new cancellation semantics (cancelled flag, immediateDelete behavior, reschedule cancel-then-reschedule flow) despite significant behavioral changes to reminder lifecycle in emailReminderManager, smsReminderManager, and booking handlers

In emailReminderManager.ts:234 and smsReminderManager.ts:187, errors are surfaced via console.log rather than the app's logger (logger/log.error used elsewhere), so cancellation failures won't appear in structured logs/alerting — critical since these functions are called fire-and-forget

goldens.comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In scheduleEmailReminders.ts:48-77, if client.request throws for any single reminder, the catch swallows the error and Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete) is never reached, so all DB deletions for that run are skipped — cancelled rows are re-processed every run and reminders whose send time arrives before a successful run will still be sent

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation block wraps a `for ... of` loop with `await client.request(...)` inside a single `try`. If any single `client.request` throws, control jumps to `catch` and `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` is skipped entirely. Because the Prisma `delete(...)` calls are only pushed into an array and never awaited/executed outside that `try`, none of the DB deletions for that run will occur, leaving `cancelled: true` rows to be re-fetched on subsequent runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In scheduleEmailReminders.ts:43, the cancellation window is scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour but this endpoint is the only thing that actually cancels 'cancelled' email reminders at SendGrid; if the cron/endpoint doesn't run or runs late, a reminder marked cancelled: true will still be sent when its send time arrives — the cancel is only advisory until the batch job executes

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` to *not* cancel the SendGrid scheduled send in the normal case; instead it just updates the DB record (`prisma.workflowReminder.update({ data: { cancelled: true } })`) unless `immediateDelete` is passed (emailReminderManager.ts). The only new code that actually calls SendGrid to cancel for these `cancelled: true` reminders is in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, and it only processes rows with `scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour`. That means a cancelled booking’s email reminder can remain scheduled in SendGrid and will still send unless/ until this endpoint runs in time to cancel it (or uses the `immediateDelete` path, which most call sites in the diff do not).

adjudication_records.issue_text: In emailReminderManager.ts:210-222, the immediateDelete path (used by workflow deletion and step deletion) cancels the reminder at SendGrid but never deletes the DB record due to an early return, leaving orphaned WorkflowReminder rows that accumulate forever

adjudication.rationale: In `emailReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete)` returns early on the `immediateDelete` path after canceling via SendGrid (`if (immediateDelete) { await client.request(...cancel...); return; }`), and does not delete or mark the `WorkflowReminder` row. The PR also removed the prior Prisma `deleteMany` cleanup in workflow/step deletion flows (e.g. `workflows.tsx` now calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` without any DB delete afterward), so those rows can remain orphaned indefinitely. The new cleanup in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` only targets rows with `cancelled: true`, which the `immediateDelete` path never sets.

adjudication_records.issue_text: On reschedule, email reminders are cancelled with immediateDelete: true (SendGrid cancel, no DB delete) while SMS reminders go through deleteScheduledSMSReminder which cancels Twilio and deletes the DB row — asymmetric handling leaves the old booking's email reminder rows in the DB pointing at a booking that no longer exists

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: on reschedule (`handleNewBooking.ts`), email reminders call `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` while SMS calls `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)`. In `emailReminderManager.ts`, the `immediateDelete` branch cancels via SendGrid and then `return`s without deleting or even marking the `WorkflowReminder` row as `cancelled`; by contrast, `smsReminderManager.ts` always deletes the DB row after (optionally) canceling Twilio. This asymmetric behavior leaves stale email reminder rows in the DB (and they also won't be picked up by the new cleanup in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, which only processes rows with `cancelled: true`).

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts the try/catch wraps a synchronous forEach that calls async functions without awaiting, so it’s true the outer try/catch won’t catch async rejections. However, the diff shows deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder both wrap their logic in internal try/catch blocks and do not rethrow, so failures won’t become unhandled promise rejections as the finding claims. The specific assertion that rejections go unhandled and the log.error path ‘never fires for actual failures’ isn’t verifiably correct from this diff (errors are already swallowed/logged inside the reminder managers).

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx` (event type disable flow), the prior DB deletion used `ctx.prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany({ where: { id: reminder.id, booking: { userId: ctx.user.id }}})` (explicit ownership scoping), but the refactor removed that and now calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)`. In the managers, deletion/update is done solely by `id` (e.g., `prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId }})` or `update({ where: { id: reminderId }, data: { cancelled: true }})`) with no user/booking ownership constraint. Whether this becomes an actual security/correctness bug depends on the (not-shown) upstream query guaranteeing only the current user's reminders; the diff verifies the loss of defense-in-depth.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts the new cancellation block iterates `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` and does `await client.request(...)` inside the loop, which makes the external cancellation calls run sequentially. Only the Prisma deletes are parallelized via collecting `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` promises and `await Promise.all(...)`. This is a diff-grounded performance/concurrency concern (slower endpoint when many reminders exist); the “widening the race window” aspect is plausible but not strictly provable from the diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces substantial new reminder-cancellation behavior (e.g., new `cancelled` column + migration/schema changes; `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?)` now sometimes marks `cancelled: true` instead of deleting; `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` adds logic to find `cancelled: true` reminders within 1 hour and cancel/delete them; booking/reschedule handlers now call the new APIs). The PR diff does not show any added/updated test files or assertions covering these new semantics/flows, so the finding about missing tests is specific and grounded in the changes shown.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` catch blocks using `console.log(...)` (emailReminderManager.ts and smsReminderManager.ts) rather than a structured logger. These functions are invoked without `await` in several places in the diff (e.g., `updatedBookings.forEach(...){ deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...) }` in handleCancelBooking.ts and similar `forEach` calls in viewer routers), so failures may be effectively silent in the app’s normal logging/alerting pipeline. This is an observability/operational concern grounded in the diff, not a direct functional defect.
